item.title: Vikings, Chiefs and Cowboys beaten - NFL week eight
item.description: The Minnesota Vikings became the last NFL team to lose their unbeaten record as the 2026 season continued with a wild weekend. There were a number of rare occurrences during week eight while two games were settled in overtime. The Dallas Cowboys and the Kansas City Chiefs were both beaten after being stunned by late fightbacks while quarterback Joe Burrow was involved in six touchdowns as the Cincinnati Bengals won again. Otherwise running backs shone on Sunday, especially for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as they managed to claim victory without completing a single pass. And the Baltimore Ravens lost not one but two quarterbacks during their defeat by the Buffalo Bills, including the league's two-time Most Valuable Player, Lamar Jackson. Here are the top stories from Sunday's action in the NFL. Jackson returns - but immediately injured again Lamar Jackson sustained his latest injury when his hand struck an opponent after throwing the ball [Getty Images] Two former MVPs went head-to-head as Lamar Jackson returned from three games out with an ankle injury to face Josh Allen's Buffalo Bills. But that match-up was ruined within moments as Jackson injured his right thumb on the game's first snap, and his back-up Tyler Huntley was then ruled out in the second quarter with a toe injury. That meant they had to finish the game with undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano at quarterback and Buffalo ran out comfortable 36-10 winners. The Ravens have lost their past three games and now have a 4-4 record, and Jackson could miss the rest of the season as he is set to undergo surgery. This is the latest injury blow for Jackson. Although he is one of the most gifted players of his generation, the 29-year-old seems destined not to reach the Super Bowl during his career and the Ravens could miss out on the play-offs for a second straight year. Huntley could also be out for weeks so the Ravens will have to act fast to bring in an experienced QB or Fagnano will have to start against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday. Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 153 yards and a touchdown as Detroit (5-2) prevailed in one of several key divisional match-ups. Lions linebacker Jack Campbell was taken to hospital to be treated for a neck injury suffered while tackling tight end TJ Hockenson in the fourth quarter. The Denver Broncos (6-2) replaced the Kansas City Chiefs (5-2) at the top of the AFC West after coming from 11 points down in the final quarter to win 28-24. item.title: A world champion but 'one of us' - a city's pride in Antonelli
item.description: Manuel Fantini's eyes are wide with excitement. There's a broad grin on his face. Fantini is recalling the first time he saw Kimi Antonelli behind the wheel of a car - well, a go-kart. "When I first saw him, I said: 'Mamma mia, chi diavolo è questo?' In English that means, 'Oh Mama, who the hell is this one?'" "He was six years old. When you go to the track for the first time, it's normal you go too fast and take turns the wrong way. "But he was improving with each lap, like he'd known the track for years. At the end of that day, he was faster than the others and with a kart slower than them. Absurd! Incredible!" Fantini is speaking to BBC Sport in a small cafe in Forli, Bologna. The autumnal sun creates a glare as the light bounces off the sign of the adjacent racetrack - Galliano Park. Owned by the Fantini family for almost 30 years, it's where Antonelli first climbed into a go-kart. It had to be adapted because he wasn't tall enough to reach the throttle or brake pedals. "His priority was being better - not being faster," says Fantini. "That is the key in motorsport to be a champion. "Everyone thinks you must be fast, but the approach of Kimi is the correct approach. "He had something immediately in his veins that was not normal. If you're only fast, you can hurt yourself or make mistakes." A former racer himself, Fantini says he is proud to have been a small part in Antonelli's journey to becoming Formula 1's youngest world champion. He is sure the 20-year-old's achievement will lift the whole country - but even more so the people of Bologna, where Antonelli was born and still visits regularly. "I am very proud of him," says Fantini. "And I'm very proud of his parents because the most difficult thing nowadays is when you have so much talent, to keep the kid safe and with humility. "I see the same incredible person. He is so natural, so funny and good as a kid. But when he puts on the helmet… pay attention." Antonelli - the boy 'born in a garage' who started driving on dad's lap Kimi Antonelli with Bologna restaurant owners Roberto and Luca Bugamelli [BBC] It has been 73 years since Italy had a Formula 1 drivers' champion. For a country synonymous with speed, it's been a torturous experience. Perhaps the highlight of Antonelli's season was winning the Italian Grand Prix from 19th on the grid - showing the mastery and bravery many predict will mean he dominates the sport for years to come. After victory at Monza, Antonelli was pictured eating pasta out of his winner's trophy. The dish - tagliatelle al ragu - was a nod to his Bolognese roots and a region famed for its cuisine. About an hour from Forli is Bologna's city centre. Down a side street is Trattoria dal Biassanot - a restaurant in which Antonelli regularly dines. item.title: Steelers’ Jaylen Warren Reacts to His Unforgettable Birthday Against The Browns
item.description: Jaylen Warren and the Pittsburgh Steelers got their revenge on the Cleveland Browns , and they did it on the same day as the running back’s birthday. Warren turned 28 years old on Sunday, and he celebrated it with a performance to remember for a long time. The former Oklahoma State Cowboys star running back tied a career high with 143 rushing yards and a touchdown on just 17 carries. That checks out for an incredibly efficient average of 8.4 yards per carry in a 27-6 win over Cleveland at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh. Birthday Celebrant Warren Speaks Up on His Big Performance in Steelers’ Win Over The Browns Nov 1, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers running back Jaylen Warren (30) reacts after scoring a touchdown during the third quarter of an NFL game against the Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images In a postgame interview with CBS Sports , Warren talked about the game that he just had. “Man, just run through anybody in my way. We knew it was going to be a gritty game coming in, and so that’s what we expected. And we just came in and executed,” Warren said. Warren also praised the chemistry of the team, particularly between the running backs and the offensive line. “We’re all on the same page. And there’s no little tweak that nobody else doesn’t understand. We’re all on the same page, seeing eye to eye to everything. And that’s why we put up the numbers we put up today,” added Warren, who is in his fifth season in the NFL. Moreover, Warren credited the work done by Pittsburgh’s stop unit against Cleveland. “Best defense in the nation. I wouldn’t want to have any other defense. We hype each other up. It’s reciprocated, and that’s what matters, and that’s what makes us great,” continued Warren. Pittsburgh had the Browns’ attack in a chokehold, as the Steelers avenged their loss to Cleveland earlier in the season . Deshaun Watson passed for 324 yards, but he never found the end zone. He was also sacked eight times for a loss of 41 yards. Warren can further celebrate his birthday in the coming days, as Pittsburgh now get to enjoy a much-deserved bye before hitting the field again in Week 10 versus the Cincinnati Bengals on the road. item.title: Antonelli proves doubters wrong as he becomes F1's youngest champion
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Italian Formula One driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli of team Mercedes celebrates with champagne on the podium after winning the Italian Grand Prix at the Autodromo Nazionale Monza in Italy. (is associated with: «Antonelli proves doubters wrong as he becomes F1's youngest champion») Bradley Collyer/PA Wire/dpa After Kimi Antonelli completed his debut Formula One season at the end of 2025, he wasn't exactly seen Mercedes' safest bet for a first drivers' title since 2020 - when Lewis Hamilton sealed a record-equalling seventh championship. The Italian claimed his first three podiums, but failed to score in 10 races and Mercedes faced calls to replace the young driver, having promoted him after just three seasons in junior single-seaters. "He wins the junior formula, then a difficult year in Formula Two and that's already where people started to doubt. People were doubters," Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff said. "People said he shouldn't even be in F1, he should be at a smaller team, 10 races and no points," Wolff added, recalling that two sponsors left the team "because who is this kid?" But on Sunday at the Mexican Grand Prix, Antonelli proved all the doubters wrong and completed a remarkable turnaround from his debut campaign to claim his maiden world title and become F1's youngest-ever champion. The race was won by Max Verstappen of Red Bull, but third place was enough for Antonelli, who needed to finish at least ninth to wrap up the championship - which became a matter of a time following such a dominant year with nine victories in 19 races so far. "Very early on, we had such a strong car, and we were very consistent and put in the performance. I thought that we could have had a shot this year, and I'm really happy that we managed to clinch it all," the newly-crowned world champion said. "It's starting to get real, and I'm going to enjoy every bit of it. I'm going to go all out with my family, friends, and the team. And we're just going to enjoy it all the way, because this is a very special moment, one that we'll remember forever." Monza: From practice nightmare to epic win Before becoming a full-time Mercedes driver, Antonelli made his first practice debut on home soil: at the 2024 Italian Grand Prix in Monza. It ended after 10 minutes following a thumping crash into the barriers at the Albareto turn. But the track where many started raising eyebrows, was where Antonelli showed an epic display of talent this year and made it clear he wasn't just a kid with a dream, but a driver with the necessary tools to win a world championship. He delivered an epic recovery from 19th to first to win this season's race in Monza - becoming the first Italian to win at the Temple of Speed since 1966. His maiden F1 title also marked the first time an Italian was crowned world champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953. item.title: Hibs toast win over Hearts - but will they kick on before cup final?
item.description: Hibs players joined their fans in a stirring rendition of Sunshine On Leith [PA Media] "I want music, I want beer." Such were Marink Reedijk's wishes, shared in an official Hibernian video from the dressing room following their historic Hampden beating of Heart of Midlothian in the Scottish League Cup semi-final. If the Hibs head coach ventured into Leith on Sunday night he would not have been short of offers for both, as he has instantly scribbled his name into the history books. His wait for a first win in charge ended at game five. As player of the match Joe Newell said afterwards: "I would have taken four losses if this was the way it clicked." There was a wee wait for Reedjik to break his Hibs duck, but that is nothing compared to the agony Hibs supporters had endured since 2006 when travelling across the M8 to face their city rivals at the national stadium. Four visits, four endings with jubilant Jambos. Until now. The sights and sounds of Sunshine on Leith being belted from the east end of the national stadium will take some time to shift, for this is a win Hibs must savour. Self-professed "ice king" Reedijk revelled in the iconic anthem but admitted it is his responsibility to make "rational decisions" and so remove himself from the "lovely atmosphere". He will know he and his players must make this moment the launchpad as they attempt to lift off the bottom of the Scottish Premiership. After he has enjoyed the tunes and pints, of course. Hibs edge Hearts in thrilling derby to reach League Cup final Giant curiosity Hibs finally liberated from the sucker punch McInnes demands more after delivering Rangers' trophy chance From 'here we go' to hardworking Hibees Who could have thought it would have played out this way? On the eve of their big trip west, Hibs had slipped - again - to the foot of the league table after Kilmarnock picked up a point at home to the 10 men of St Johnstone. A shocking place for this squad to be, but it was - temporarily - rendered meaningless 24 hours later. Given their turbulent start to the season - missing out on Europe, failing to win at home and changing managers - being backed by 19,000 supporters was something in itself. Finally, they were rewarded. Those who travelled to Warsaw last year to lose out on goal difference to Legia and returned from Gent in August with an abundance of hope only to have it dashed at Easter Road, had their moment of joy. And they rightly milked it. item.title: Arsenal suffered another injury issue pre-Liverpool
item.description: Arsenal suffered another injury issue pre-Liverpool Mikel Arteta has revealed that Eberechi Eze had an injury issue ahead of Sunday’s game against Liverpool, increasing the importance of Christos Tzolis’ return. Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images Arsenal fans were somewhat surprised to see Christos Tzolis in the starting lineup against Liverpool over the weekend, as the player was only making his first appearance in the squad after weeks out injured. But Mikel Arteta explained afterwards that part of the problem was a new injury issue for left-wing alternative option Eberechi Eze . “We had an issue with Ebs as well,” Arteta revealed . “It was incredible that he was in the squad today. I want to give credit to all the medical and the performance team because what they’re doing with those boys is incredible, every three days to keep everybody at this level. “That’s why these are the margins sometimes where you win a football match and not when you have somebody available or not.” Photo by Leonhard Simon/Getty Images As mentioned, Eze was in the squad for the match, and he spent much of the contest warming up on the sidelines, so the hope is that he’ll be back to full fitness very shortly. Then the good news with the returning Tzolis was that he came through the match without any issues, despite immediately returning to the starting lineup and playing most of the 90. He was only eventually substituted with six minutes to play. “With Christos it’s incredible,” Arteta said. “He didn’t want to come off; he wanted to complete the game. We took some risks and at that point we decided, now is enough.” Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images With Eze and Tzolis both available, Arsenal will have options on the left again. Ceadach O’Neill also travelled with the squad for the Liverpool game as the extra man, and he might get chances at times too. On the other side, Arsenal are a little reliant on Noni Madueke , with Bukayo Saka injured and Max Dowman suspended. Dowman will at least be available for the midweek game against Slavia Praha , as his three-game ban only applies domestically. Photo by Lewis Storey/Getty Images

item.title: ‘Not Buffalo Bills…’ – Analyst makes bold Angel Reese and Dream prediction for 2027 WNBA Finals
item.description: Photo by Heather Diehl/Getty Images One WNBA analyst is already backing the Atlanta Dream for the 2027 WNBA Finals. The Atlanta Dream had no answer for the Golden State Valkyries in Game 7 of the tightly fought 2026 WNBA Finals. The Valkyries managed to keep star forward Angel Reese in check as she was held to just eight points in the 68-63 defeat for the Dream. It was the complete opposite, as the Baltimore Ravens superstar two-way quarterback lasted just a snap in Sunday’s marquee matchup against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills at the new Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park, New York. Jackson had his right hand struck by Buffalo linebacker Greg Rousseau as the two-time NFL Most Valuable Player was trying to make a pass. That led to Jackson later leaving the field with a banged-up finger. Here is a look at that finger injury, as shown on the broadcast while he was leaving the field to get checked on. item.description: New York Jets rookie Omar Cooper Jr. was among the fantasy football darlings heading into Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season. But he was barely felt on the field during Sunday’s game between the Jets and the Las Vegas Raiders at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford. Cooper, who suffered an ankle injury in Week 1 and missed four games before returning to action in Week 6, had many excited for him entering the Raiders game. After all, he had at least 100 receiving yards in each of the two games heading into the meeting with Las Vegas. He posted 103 receiving yards and a touchdown on six receptions in a Week 6 loss to the New England Patriots. He followed that up with a 115-yard effort plus a touchdown on five catches in a 28-25 loss to the Miami Dolphins in Week 7. But against the Raiders, the former Indiana Hoosiers star wide receiver didn’t catch a pass and wasn’t even targeted as New York suffered a 38-33 loss. item.title: Russell’s Media No-Show Cost Mercedes €5,000. Wolff Calls It ‘Understandable’
item.description: George Russell skipped his media duties after Kimi Antonelli clinched the F1 title in Mexico, earning Mercedes a fine, but Toto Wolff defended him. Having qualified on the front row, it was another disaster for Mercedes’ Russell at the start of the F1 Mexico GP. He had a good initial launch, but then slowed immediately , which dropped him outside the top five. It left him distraught, and Mercedes F1 team boss Wolff had to apologize on the radio . In a bid to recover places, he made contact with Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar, which sent the Frenchman spinning. The Brit was handed a 10-second time penalty as a result. Mercedes Fined for Russell Even though he put in a solid defense against McLaren’s Lando Norris in the first stint, he was undone by the penalty as he emerged behind him after the pit stop. He finished sixth, as the F1 title went to teammate Kimi Antonelli . Russell made sure to congratulate the Italian under the podium, but then left the circuit without attending the mandatory post-race media duties. He also missed the stewards’ hearing that followed, with a team representative giving evidence by telephone. As a result, Mercedes was fined 5,000 euros . Wolff, meanwhile, defended Russell for skipping the duties. The Austrian understands the emotional state the Brit would be in after a season he has had. After how the Mexico GP start panned out, it was a race lost for him as well, on top of the F1 title loss. Photo by Sam Bloxham/LAT Images Wolff Defends Russell for Skipping Media Duties “I saw George after the race on the FIA scales,” Wolff said to the media after the F1 Mexico GP. “And obviously he’s distraught about the situation. It was a great show of sportsmanship to go and see Kimi. I have known George for such a long time, and I know for a sports person, he is going through a hard time, but he was also responsible in getting the young man into this team. “So I saw him in that. For a racing driver, this is a catastrophic moment. And maybe today the race was a little bit of a picture of his season. This was a race for him to win. We had the pace in the car. And we let him down on the first straight. The energy delivery is not what we had thought it should be. “So, I’m very much with him at the moment. I’ve been in situations where it’s very, very difficult to cope. So, him not doing the media work or leaving the track is absolutely understandable. Him staying would have actually surprised me. So that’s absolutely all,” summed up Wolff. For Russell, the chance to defend second in the F1 championship gets even tougher. He has dropped behind Max Verstappen (261) and Lewis Hamilton (259) to be fourth with 250 points. Also, Charles Leclerc (245) is only five behind. item.title: Ravens reportedly interested in trading for veteran quarterback
item.description: Charles LeClaire-USA TODAY Sports The Baltimore Ravens’ season took a devastating turn on Sunday, when star quarterback Lamar Jackson injured his throwing thumb on the first play of a 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills. Now, with backup Tyler Huntley also banged up, the Ravens could reportedly turn to the trade market for help. According to one report, the Ravens could be targeting a veteran quarterback to help shore up the position, but it sounds like they’ll have to be ready to spend. Ravens’ Quarterback Injuries Jackson, who had just returned from a three-game absence due to an ankle injury, was hurt when his right hand struck Bills pass rusher Greg Rousseau on a throw. He headed to the locker room and later returned to the sideline with his hand in a cast. After the game, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed that Jackson will undergo surgery and be placed on injured reserve. Asked whether the injury could end Jackson’s season, Minter said, “potentially.” “It’s tough,” Minter said. “When it happened, I think at the time, you’re just hoping that maybe it’s something small, and then I think pretty quickly kind of realized what had happened.” To make matters worse, Huntley suffered a toe injury in the second quarter, forcing undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano into his NFL debut. The UConn product went 10-of-21 for 91 yards with an interception. ‘It Won’t Be Cheap’ According to a report from Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk, the Ravens are looking into trading for Chicago Bears quarterback Tyson Bagent. “The Ravens, we’re told, may explore the possibility of acquiring Bagent,” Florio of Pro Football Talk reported . “We’re also told that it won’t be cheap to get him.” Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle held the same position with the Bears last season, so he’s familiar with Bagent. Chicago also has three quarterbacks under contract, with Bagent and Case Keenum backing up starter Caleb Williams, so they could be willing to move one of them. That said, Florio warns that acquiring Bagent won’t be cheap. “That’s how it goes when a team develops an in-season need for a quarterback,” Florio wrote. “The price goes up, as reflected by the urgency of the effort to find a replacement.” We’ll have to see whether or not the Ravens make this move. item.title: Kimi Antonelli reveals why he won’t take number 1 for the 2027 F1 season
item.description: Motorsport photo The number 1 will not be seen on the Formula 1 grid next season for the first time since 2021. Max Verstappen and Lando Norris have consistently decided to take the opportunity to claim number 1 after winning their world titles, but Antonelli will not do so. Asked by Motorsport.com whether he would switch to number 1 or whether number 12 held such special meaning for him that he wanted to keep it, he explained after the race in Mexico: “I think I'll stay with number 12. "I'll stay with number 12 because, obviously, it's a very special number for me”, Antonelli said shortly after replacing Sebastian Vettel as the youngest world champion of all time. The number 12 is a tribute to Antonelli's idol Ayrton Senna and was also the first number he used in single-seaters, in Formula 4. Another nice detail is that Antonelli is also the first driver since Senna in 1988 to clinch the F1 world title with the number 12. Beyond this special meaning, Antonelli has a second reason for keeping number 12, one that reflects who he is as a person. “It's also a way for me to stay grounded, to stay humble. I feel like keeping number 12 allows me to have a new point where to start and to build on everything again and try to improve more.” His modesty has proved to be an important quality on several occasions this year. Even after his impressive performance in Austin, when asked by this website how he manages to cope so well with the pressure at such a young age, Antonelli was particularly keen to give credit to his family and the people at Mercedes instead of himself. Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Besides the value he attaches to number 12, Antonelli indicated that he has not had good experiences with the number 1, providing another reason not to make the switch. “To be honest, I'm very superstitious and number one has never been a good number for me. Whenever I put it [on], it went extremely badly!” Antonelli laughed. “So that’s one more reason to stay with number 12.” That superstition also played a role for Antonelli during the race weekend in Mexico, as he revealed in the post-race press conference. It meant he absolutely did not want to think the title was already in the bag, as he feared he might jinx the outcome. “I kept hearing the same thing over and over again”, Antonelli said, referring, according to Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff, to the fact that many people had already congratulated him prematurely on winning the world title on Friday. “And, you know, I'm quite straightforward on this: until it's done, it's not done. So, I knew that I still wanted to finish the job well, and it's not easy when you keep hearing from many people, guests, fans, congratulations for the championship. “Knowing myself, I'm very superstitious. item.title: James Milner stuns fans with incredible New York Marathon time as Liverpool & Man City icon proves he is still a fitness machine at 40
item.description: Alfred Dunhill Links Championship - Previews - Getty Images Sport James Milner has long been regarded as one of the most dedicated professionals in the history of the Premier League, and he has now proven that his legendary engine is still running at full throttle. The former England international took on the gruelling New York Marathon this weekend, delivering a highly impressive performance on his debut over the 42.125-kilometre distance. Former midfielder shines in New York After calling time on his extensive two-decade football career this summer , Milner tested his renowned fitness levels on the famous New York course. The 40-year-old crossed the finish line with an impressive time of three hours, nine minutes, and four seconds. Tackling a route known more for testing hills than rapid finishes, the former Brighton and Aston Villa man recorded an average pace of seven minutes and 12 seconds per mile, which equates to roughly four minutes and 28 seconds per kilometre. Staying true to his pre-race strategy, Milner started aggressively instead of running a measured race. He cleared the first half in one hour and 31 minutes before battling through the latter stages to complete the second half in one hour and 38 minutes. Knee issues nearly scuppered running ambitions Ahead of his first world major, Milner admitted that his primary obstacle was "building up the mileage without getting injured", especially since his previous clubs had restricted his running workload late in his career. The Englishman also acknowledged that a faster time might have been possible in his younger days. "A few years ago, I feel like I could have definitely done sub-3:00," he explained. "My career went on longer and longer. Two years ago, I had a knee operation, and when I woke up from the knee operation, I couldn’t lift my foot. And I had a second operation that day to check, and then I couldn’t lift my foot for six months. I had nerve damage. "So I feel to go from not being able to walk properly and maybe never being able to walk to coming back, playing football in the Premier League, and hopefully potentially finishing a marathon, I don’t want to get too much caught up on the time." Premier League pedigree translates to the road Milner's seamless transition to long-distance running will surprise very few. During his time at Liverpool, he was famous for dominating the club's gruelling pre-season lactate threshold sessions, consistently outlasting his team-mates until they collapsed from exhaustion. He also possessed a strong childhood background in cross-country running. While his debut time is excellent, he sits slightly behind fellow former professionals in the marathon standings. item.title: 'That’s not a penalty' - Jose Mourinho slams VAR inconsistency after Real Madrid spot-kick controversy
item.description: Real Racing Club de Santander v Real Madrid - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Real Madrid secured a comfortable 3-0 victory over Racing Santander, but the match was heavily overshadowed by a controversial penalty decision involving Kylian Mbappe. Jose Mourinho and former referee Eduardo Iturralde Gonzalez have both heavily criticised the lack of VAR intervention during the incident. Real Madrid cruise to victory Madrid secured a comfortable 3-0 victory over Racing Santander at El Sardinero. However, the comprehensive away win was overshadowed by a highly controversial penalty decision involving Mbappe. A spot-kick was awarded following an incident involving the French forward. The decision immediately sparked debate, with critics questioning the legitimacy of the foul and the glaring lack of intervention from the video assistant referee. Mourinho questions VAR decision Mourinho was quick to offer his assessment of the controversial incident. The manager revealed he reviewed the footage on a tablet and immediately felt a clear error had been made by the officials. "They change them so much, and the small details are such that people don’t know that it’s never a penalty by [Aurelien] Tchouameni because of the rebound from the ball," Mourinho explained on the club's official website . "It’s never a penalty. When the referee called a penalty, I stayed calm because from 60 meters away, I couldn’t see it. But later, when I saw it on the iPad, I thought, if VAR doesn’t mess up, that’s not a penalty. "For me, the referee was technically very good and disciplined. He gave out a couple of yellow cards, and that’s it. It was a tough and competitive match. For me, it’s obvious that it wasn’t a penalty." Ex-referee demands more consistency Former referee Gonzalez completely agreed with Mourinho's damning assessment. He strongly criticised the lack of consistency from the VAR officials, comparing the incident to a similar situation in the match between Getafe and Sevilla earlier in the day. "If the VAR has intervened in Getafe-Sevilla for a hand to the face, it has to intervene for this; otherwise, there is no refereeing consistency," Iturralde Gonzalez argued, as quoted by Mundo Deportivo . He was left baffled by the differing standards applied across the two matches in such a short space of time. He concluded: "Why in one hour has it intervened in Getafe and not in Santander in a very, very similar action? For me, it is not a penalty." Focus on the upcoming matches The controversial penalty ultimately helped Madrid secure all three points on their travels. item.title: Real Madrid captain returns to training ahead of AEK Athens clash
item.description: Real Madrid captain returns to training ahead of AEK Athens clash Real Madrid have received a timely boost after confirming on their website that Federico Valverde has returned to training with the first-team squad ahead of their upcoming fixture against AEK Athens. The midfielder missed the 3-0 victory over Racing Santander after experiencing discomfort during the Clasico against Barcelona, but his return to group training offers Jose Mourinho an important option during a demanding period. With Real Madrid facing multiple matches before the November international break, Valverde’s recovery could prove particularly valuable as the manager looks to maintain his team’s momentum without placing unnecessary strain on key players. Valverde returns after missing Racing Santander match Valverde experienced discomfort during the first half of Real Madrid’s victory over Barcelona and eventually came off in the second period. Although initial assessments ruled out a serious injury , the Uruguayan was unable to resume normal training with his teammates ahead of the Racing Santander fixture. Valverde has returned to team training. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) There had been optimism that the captain would recover in time for Sunday’s match, but the coaching staff ultimately decided against risking him. His absence was noticeable given his importance to Mourinho’s midfield, although Real Madrid still secured a convincing 3-0 victory at El Sardinero. His return to group training therefore is an encouraging development ahead of Wednesday’s European assignment. However, completing a training session with the squad does not automatically guarantee that he will be ready to start. Mourinho receives boost before AEK Athens test Real Madrid travel to face AEK Athens in the UEFA Champions League on Wednesday, November 4, and Valverde’s availability would give Mourinho greater flexibility when selecting his midfield. Valverde missed the Racing game. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) The manager may nevertheless consider managing the Uruguayan’s workload carefully, particularly after the discomfort he experienced against Barcelona. With an important fixture against Valencia scheduled next, there is little incentive to rush him back if he is not fully comfortable. Notably, Valverde has been operating as Mourinho’s preferred right-back in recent matches, but in his absence against Racing, Trent Alexander-Arnold played the full game. This means everything points to Denzel Dumfries starting the match against AEK Athens, potentially leaving Valverde to come on if the game requires.

Their biggest result so far, quite clearly, was the win over Barcelona last weekend. A brace by Kylian Mbappe saw Los Blancos take all three points from the Spotify Camp Nou, and the big question was whether the team could keep the momentum going. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) The player first opened up about how it was refreshing to see Real Madrid dominate games from the get-go once again and how the team is now very organised. “It’s been a long time since I’ve seen Madrid dominate the opening 20 minutes like that. Everyone is in their position, and everyone tracks back and does their defensive duties when required,” he said, as quoted by Defensa Central . He then specifically praised Jude Bellingham for the player that he is, and highlighted how he is a stellar goalscorer. “Bellingham is so good at making runs into the box. What a player! item.title: Liverpool fail to register a shot on target at Anfield for the first time in Premier League history
item.description: Liverpool fail to register a shot on target at Anfield for the first time in Premier League history Liverpool failed to land a single shot on target at Anfield as Arsenal ground out a 1-0 win, a first for the Reds at home in the Premier League era. Andoni Iraola 's side attempted 17 shots on Sunday, according to Sky Sports , yet David Raya never had to make a save. Kai Havertz's tap-in in the 16th minute proved decisive. Liverpool had never before played a Premier League match at Anfield without a shot on target, since the data was first collected in 2003/04. It came despite Andoni Iraola starting all of Liverpool's £100m+ recruits, as Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola featured from the start. The result handed Arsenal their first victory at Anfield since September 2012, a milestone Mikel Arteta celebrated after full-time, as the Spaniard hailed a 'historic' win . Woodwork, wayward headers and no penalty Liverpool's best moments came at the end of the first half. Florian Wirtz curled a free-kick onto the crossbar, and Alexis Mac Allister, unmarked, headed a Milos Kerkez cross over the bar. After the break Isak fired over from a tight angle, while Ronald Araujo had an effort blocked by Arsenal bodies. Substitute Victor Munoz got his head to a Kostas Tsimikas cross late on, which was the hosts' last chance. The biggest grievance was a first-half shirt pull by Jurrien Timber on Isak inside the box. The officials gave nothing, with both Iraola and Virgil van Dijk critical of the decision at full-time. Arsenal's chances were limited but cleaner. Alisson produced a fine stop to deny Christos Tzolis in the second half. By the closing stages, Liverpool were reduced to using Virgil van Dijk as an emergency centre-forward. The defeat was Liverpool's second under Iraola and ended a five-game winning run in all competitions. It leaves them fifth, nine points behind Arsenal, who sit three clear of Manchester City at the top. Iraola pointed to his side's slow start in his post-match briefing: "Overall, I think we have to blame especially the start of the game and until we conceded the goal."

item.title: Oleksandr Usyk talks up shock fight with feared champion at old weight
item.description: Oleksandr Usyk has talked up a showdown with feared cruiserweight champion David Benavidez , in a shocking potential next move. After surviving a scare against kickboxing icon Rico Verhoeven in the boxing ring in May, Usyk vacated the unified heavyweight titles and claimed his next bout would be his last. Now, however, the unbeaten Ukrainian has suggested he might have an extra fight in him, with the second of those two contests ideally coming against Benavidez. Usyk is a two-time undisputed heavyweight champion, but he made his name at cruiserweight, where he became the only undisputed champion of the four-belt era. The 39-year-old was expected to round out his career at heavyweight, potentially against former champion Deontay Wilder , but he seems adamant about a surprising weight-cut to his old division. “Because I cleaned out the heavyweight [division] and [want to go] back to my weight,” Usyk told The Ring on Saturday. “Yes, correct, [I want to fight the best version of Benavidez]. “Right now, I weigh 96 or 97 kg [211-213lb]. If I have an opportunity at cruiserweight, I am back. It’s a big fight because Benavidez is a big champion. Me, a little bit, too?” Also at the weekend, Usyk’s team director Sergey Lapin told Casinostugan : “First, we are looking at a fight for a vacant world title.
